nindian-economy-48-3.s: A decrease in the Capital-Output Ratio means that, per unit of output:
nindian-economy-48-3.x: A lower COR means less capital is needed per unit of output, which raises growth potential.

n8a86bcdf6e3.s: Under the Second Five Year Plan, Chittaranjan was associated with the manufacture of:
n8a86bcdf6e3.x: Chittaranjan made locomotives; Perambur made coaches and Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were steel plants.

n6fec6a6d0e4.s: Which of the following did the Bombay Plan (1944) favour?
o: A significant role for the State
n6fec6a6d0e4.x: The Bombay Plan wanted a significant State role, public sector development and protection of infant industries.

nindian-economy-22-5.s:
Consider the following statements about India's planning milestones:
1. The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938.
2. The Bombay and Gandhian Plans came in 1944.
3. The People's Plan came before the Bombay Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nindian-economy-22-5.x: The NPC dates to 1938 and the Bombay and Gandhian Plans to 1944; the People's Plan came later, in 1945.

n5c65646f390.s: Doubling of per capita income in ten years was an aim of which Five Year Plan?
n5c65646f390.x: The Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and sought to double per capita income within ten years.

nc097f2e9a63.s: Which of the following pairs of Five Year Plan and objective is correctly matched?
o: Second Plan – Growth with stability and progressive self-reliance
Fifth Plan – Self-reliant and self-generating economy
Third Plan – Self-reliant and self-generating economy
Fourth Plan – Removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao)
nc097f2e9a63.x: The Third Plan aimed at a self-reliant, self-generating economy; growth with stability was the Fourth Plan's aim.

n25662c341e4.s: The Eleventh Plan's 27 national monitorable targets included how many State-level targets?
n25662c341e4.x: The Eleventh Plan set 27 national monitorable targets, including 13 at the State level.

na1d1bb4ab8f.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 identified Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and ____ as Andhra Pradesh's three economic regions.
na1d1bb4ab8f.x: The three economic regions are Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati; Kurnool is not one of them. (No dates, so no sequence could be built.)

n7d022a58d77.s: Which of the following pairs about the outcome of planning in India is correctly matched?
n7d022a58d77.x: Land reforms were poorly implemented and unequal land ownership persisted; income inequality widened.

ndc036e54dac.s: How many banks were nationalised in 1969, during the Fourth Plan period?
ndc036e54dac.x: Fourteen banks were nationalised in 1969, during the Fourth Plan.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of plan model and its main bottleneck is correctly matched?
new.x: Harrod-Domar saw limited savings as the bottleneck; Mahalanobis saw capital goods and the wage-goods model saw food.

new.s: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) was based on which model?
new.x: The Third Plan followed the Sandy-Chakravarty model with import substitution.

new.s: The Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74) was based on the model of:
new.x: The Fourth Plan used the Allen Manne – Ashok Rudra model along with the Gadgil strategy.

new.s: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79) was based on the:
new.x: The Fifth Plan was based on the Dhar model.

new.s: Which of the following models was NOT the basis of any Indian Five Year Plan?
new.x: The neoclassical Solow-Swan model was never used by an Indian plan; the others underlay the First, Fourth and Third Plans.

new.s: In the Harrod-Domar equation g = s / k, 'k' stands for the:
new.x: In g = s / k, g is the growth rate, s the savings rate and k the capital-output ratio.

new.s: The First Five Year Plan succeeded mainly because of:
o: Good harvests in its last two years
new.x: Despite refugees, food shortage and inflation, the First Plan succeeded mainly due to good harvests in its last two years.

new.s: How many sectors did the Mahalanobis model have?
new.x: Its four sectors were capital goods, factory consumer goods, household/small-scale consumer goods and services.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahalanobis model:
1. Feldman (1928) and Mahalanobis (1953) developed it independently.
2. It left consumer goods to the small and cottage sector.
3. It gave top priority to agriculture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the model gave priority to the capital goods sector and neglected agriculture.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT neglected by the Mahalanobis model?
new.x: Heavy industry was its priority; agriculture, consumer goods and exports were neglected.

new.s: The Indian Statistical Institute was founded in Kolkata in:
new.x: P.C. Mahalanobis founded the ISI on 17 December 1931; the ISI Act came in 1959.

new.s: National Statistics Day has been observed in India since:
new.x: National Statistics Day, 29 June, has been observed since 2007.

new.s: P.C. Mahalanobis is known as the architect of which Five Year Plan?
new.x: Mahalanobis was the architect of the Second Plan (1956-61).

new.s: In the wage-goods model, more wage goods would allow which group to be put to productive work?
new.x: Vakil and Brahmananda argued that more wage goods would let the disguised unemployed be put to productive work.

new.s: In contrast to Mahalanobis, the wage-goods model held that the real constraint was NOT the supply of:
new.x: The wage-goods model saw food and essential consumer goods as the constraint, not capital goods.

new.s: The Bombay Plan (1944) aimed to raise national income how many times in 15 years?
new.x: The Bombay Plan aimed to treble national income in 15 years; the Visvesvaraya Plan aimed to double it in a decade.

new.s: How many Bombay industrialists signed the Bombay Plan?
new.x: The Bombay Plan was drawn up by 8 Bombay industrialists, including J.R.D. Tata and G.D. Birla.

new.s: The National Planning Committee (1938), set up under Subhas Chandra Bose, was chaired by:
new.x: The NPC was set up under Bose and chaired by Nehru.

new.s: 'Gandhian Constitution for Free India' was written by:
new.x: Shriman Narayan Agarwal wrote it, not M.N. Roy; Charan Singh wrote 'The Gandhian Blue Print'.

new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Planning'?
new.x: M. Visvesvaraya, whose 'Planned Economy for India' (1934) was the first planning blueprint, is called the Father of Indian Planning.

new.s: The Rolling Plan adopted by the Janata Government (1978-80) was the concept of:
new.x: The Rolling Plan, adopted after the Fifth Plan was ended a year early, was Gunnar Myrdal's concept.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about types of planning:
1. India follows indicative planning.
2. Stalin's USSR followed indicative planning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: India follows indicative planning; Stalin's USSR, which began plans in 1928, followed imperative planning.

new.s: The Drought Prone Area Programme was introduced in which Five Year Plan?
new.x: The DPAP and other target-group programmes began in the Fourth Plan.

new.s: The Minimum Needs Programme was launched in the first year of the:
new.x: The Minimum Needs Programme began in the first year of the Fifth Plan.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of programme and Five Year Plan is correctly matched?
new.x: IRDP came in the Sixth Plan; CADA was a Fifth Plan programme and Jawahar Rozgar Yojana came in the Seventh.

new.s: The Command Area Development Programme (1974-75) belongs to which Five Year Plan?
new.x: CADA was started in 1974-75, in the Fifth Plan.

new.s: The Eleventh Five Year Plan's monitorable target for Infant Mortality Rate was:
new.x: The Eleventh Plan targeted an IMR of 28; the Twelfth Plan targeted 25.

new.s: How many monitorable targets did the Twelfth Five Year Plan set?
new.x: The Twelfth Plan had 25 monitorable targets, against 27 in the Eleventh.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a target of the Eleventh Five Year Plan?
new.x: Inclusive growth relied on continued reform and a competitive private sector, not its withdrawal.

new.s: The planned public sector outlay of the Second Five Year Plan was:
new.x: The planned public outlay was Rs 4,800 crore; the actual outlay was pruned to Rs 4,600 crore.

new.s: The Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy created few jobs mainly because it relied on:
new.x: Its capital-intensive heavy industry generated few jobs, a key criticism of the strategy.

new.s: The foundation stone of Nagarjuna Sagar dam was laid by Jawaharlal Nehru in:
new.x: Nehru laid the foundation on 10 December 1955; the dam was built from 1955 to 1967.

new.s: Construction of the Srisailam power project in Andhra Pradesh began in:
new.x: Srisailam construction began in 1960 and the project opened in 1981.

new.s: Under the Telugu Ganga project, Krishna water reached Poondi (Chennai) in:
new.x: The Telugu Ganga project was taken up in the 1980s and its water reached Poondi in 2004.

new.s: During the Eleventh Plan, the share of agriculture and allied sectors in Andhra Pradesh's GSDP was:
new.x: Agriculture and allied sectors made up 21.27% of AP's GSDP in the Eleventh Plan.

new.s: For General Category States such as Andhra Pradesh, central plan assistance was given in the grant : loan ratio of:
new.x: General Category States got 30% grant and 70% loan; Special Category States got 90 : 10.

new.s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, per capita income carried a weight of:
new.x: Population had 60%, per capita income 25%, and fiscal performance and special problems 7.5% each.

new.s: Which Five Year Plan is described with the remark 'the poor became poorer'?
new.x: The Eighth Plan's record on poverty is summed up as 'the poor became poorer'.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a failure of Indian planning?
new.x: Food self-sufficiency, through the Green Revolution and FCI, was an achievement; the others were failures.

new.s: Poverty in India fell from 48.3% in 1977-78 to ____ in 1983-84.
new.x: Poverty fell from 48.3% (1977-78) to 37.4% (1983-84), an achievement of planning.

new.s: India's First Five Year Plan was launched on:
new.x: The First Plan was launched on 1 April 1951 with focus on agriculture and irrigation.

new.s: The focus sector of India's First Five Year Plan was:
new.x: The First Plan gave priority to agriculture and irrigation.

new.s: The Plan Holiday of 1966-69 followed the failure of which Five Year Plan?
new.x: The Third Plan's failure (2.2% vs 5.6%) led to the Plan Holiday of 1966-69.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the Third Plan's failure?
new.x: The Third Plan was hit by the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 droughts; the 1971 war affected the Fourth Plan.

new.s: The Fourth Five Year Plan targeted export growth of about:
new.x: The Fourth Plan's Gadgil strategy targeted exports growing about 7% a year.

new.s: Against a target of 5.7%, the Fourth Five Year Plan achieved growth of only:
new.x: The Fourth Plan achieved 3.3% against 5.7% because of droughts and the 1971 war.

new.s: Under central plan assistance, Special Category States received grant and loan in the ratio:
new.x: Special Category States got 90% grant and 10% loan; General Category got 30 : 70.

new.s: The Gadgil formula for allocating central assistance to State plans was replaced by the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula in:
new.x: The Gadgil formula (1969) gave way to the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula in 1991.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an achievement of planning in India?
new.x: Regional disparities persist and are a failure of planning, not an achievement.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about planning in India:
1. Planning is a constitutional requirement.
2. After 1991, planning became indicative, showing priority sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Planning is not a constitutional requirement; after 1991 it moved from directed to indicative.

new.s: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on:
new.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a government resolution on 1 January 2015.

new.s: Who was the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
new.x: M.S. Ahluwalia was the last Deputy Chairman before the Commission was dissolved in 2014.

new.s: The last Five Year Plan of India ended on:
new.x: The Twelfth Plan (2012-17), the last, ended on 31 March 2017.

new.s: NITI Aayog's 15-year vision document runs up to:
new.x: The 15-year vision runs up to 2030, with a 7-year strategy and 3-year action agenda.

new.s: The period of NITI Aayog's 3-year action agenda was:
new.x: The 3-year action agenda (released 1 August 2017) covered 2017-18 to 2019-20.

new.s: The 7-year strategy that replaced the Five Year Plans covered:
new.x: The 7-year strategy ran from 2017-18 to 2023-24.
